You can see what sites links go in the little grayed-out parenthesis, so if you didn't want to go somewhere you could just not click it. I really think the idea of just blocking out things you don't want to see kind of defeats the purpose of an open social medium. You can't just block out things you don't like in real life - you tolerate them and make a point not to support them. And move on.

I fear something like this would keep people out of the loop on a variety of subjects because let's say a news site has a blog piece that you don't agree with - so you block it. The site itself is newsworthy, or up-and-coming, or hosting a premier piece later in the year, but you miss out because of one article you didn't like that caused you to block the entire site.

I don't think I could support this kind of self-blinkering. It's weird, because it isn't like on Reddit where they blind you to things they don't want you to see, it's allowing yourself to block out anything that might potentially annoy you at the cost of any and every other offering from that site. There have been a lot of news sites (or satire sites) that I think I might have missed if I had had the ability to block them based off of an earlier piece I'd see on the FP. Wasn't feeling it that day, maybe the piece was poorly written or discussed a topic I wasn't interested in/disagreed with, etc. Should an entire site potentially be judged based on one (or a few) pieces. Nah.
